# Model Context Protocol

> > A standardized protocol for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools using JSON-RPC 2.0, enabling context-aware AI applications through client-server architecture.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that allows AI models to securely access context from various sources. It supports multiple transport layers (HTTP+SSE, STDIO), implements OAuth 2.1 authentication, and evolves through a community-driven Spec Enhancement Proposal (SEP) process.

## Key Topics

- Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- JSON-RPC 2.0
- Client-server architecture
- Streamable HTTP transport
- Context exchange
- OAuth 2.1 authentication
- Spec Enhancement Proposals (SEPs)
- MCP Registry
- Capability negotiation
- Tools and resources
- Protocol lifecycle
- Security best practices
- SDK development (Python, TypeScript, Rust)
- HTTP+SSE transport
- Dynamic Client Registration

## Core Specification

- [Overview - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic): MCP spec overview: JSON-RPC 2.0, HTTP/STDIO transports, lifecycle basics
- [Architecture - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/architecture): MCP architecture spec: client-server design, JSON-RPC, security boundaries
- [Lifecycle - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/lifecycle): MCP lifecycle spec: initialization, capability negotiation, handshake
- [Schema Reference - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/schema): MCP schema reference: JSON-RPC API spec, data types, ISO 8601 standards
- [Tools - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools): MCP tools spec: server capabilities, invocation, JSON-RPC messages
- [Roots - Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/client/roots): Roots spec: filesystem access, workspace config, JSON-RPC notifications
